newsitem.title: JAPAN: TEPCO sets up oil fences after Tokyo Bay oil spill.
newsitem.headline: TEPCO sets up oil fences after Tokyo Bay oil spill.

text.p: Tokyo Electric Power Co Inc (TEPCO) said on Wednesday that it has set up fences around all 11 of its thermal power plants located on Tokyo Bay as a precautionary measure after a major oil spill.
The oil fences were set up to keep away oil, which leaked from the 259,999 deadweight-tonne Panamanian-flagged Diamond Grace, from the power plants' intake pipes.
"We finished setting up the oil fences at around 4.40 p.m. (0740 GMT)," a TEPCO spokesman said.
The electric power utility has 11 thermal power plants ringing the bay, where the supertanker struck an undersea reef.
The spokesman said plant operations remained unaffected so far.
Japan's coastguard estimated that the tanker, which scraped a reef in the shallow waters of Tokyo Bay on Wednesday morning, may have leaked 13,400 tonnes of crude oil.
The vessel was heading to Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd's Kawasaki refinery, south of Tokyo, from the Middle East where it had lifted crude oil.
The intake pipe draws water from the sea to cool the steam created in the plants' boilers.
